title: Catalog certification scenarios and UX snippets lab
body:
Purpose:
This is a working lab for the marketplace/catalog certification scenarios we keep hitting in partner onboarding. Goal: produce a concise acceptance matrix + UX copy snippets that engineering, legal, and design can iterate on quickly. This doc intentionally mixes explicit checklist items with informal notes and copy experiments. Treat as a living scratchpad until we lock a final runbook in Confluence.

Audience:
- GTM product owners and program managers running the publisher path
- Partner engineering and integration leads
- Design/UX for tile + detail page copy
- Security/compliance owners who must sign off on gating items

How to use this lab:
1) Read the scenarios for the certification tier that matches the partner (SMB vs enterprise).
2) Pick the copy variant(s) for tile + short description we want to run in the listing A/B tests.
3) Follow the checklist, mark items with Jira keys, and loop in owners.

Quick note to self: this should be shorter than the big Confluence playbook; keep it pragmatic for first 2 releases (AWS/GCP).

Certification scenarios (high level):
- Scenario A: Self-serve SaaS (SMB-friendly)
  - Requirements: sandboxed demo, public docs, basic support email, billing via marketplace. No VPC/VPN.
  - Security gates: privacy policy link, vulnerability disclosure, basic SSO guide (OAuth).
  - Acceptance criteria: tile copy emphasizes "quick start" and "free trial", SLO target for onboarding flow declared.

- Scenario B: Enterprise-ready (SLA + Dedicated)
  - Requirements: enterprise onboarding checklist, SOC2 or attestations, SSO (SAML/OIDC), KMS integration docs, contract/legal contact.
  - Security gates: KMS/HSM references, network topology diagram for private deployment, encryption-at-rest detail.
  - Acceptance criteria: QA note that listing must include "Private deployment available" and link to architecture PDF.

- Scenario C: Hybrid/On-prem (regulated workloads)
  - Requirements: downloadable installer or container image, air-gapped deployment guidance, on-prem support plan.
  - Security gates: offline key management instructions, audit log export format, end-to-end test plan with customer sample data (redacted).

Checklist (acceptance matrix) — quick view (mark DONE/INPROGRESS/OPEN in Jira):
- Product metadata: tile title, short description, long description (owner: PM)
- Billing: marketplace SKU mapping, free trial SKU, trial length (owner: finance)
- Docs: quickstart, admin guide, integration guide (owner: techdocs)
- Security: SSO guide + encryption, SOC2/Known attestations (owner: security)
- Legal: terms of service alignment, data processing addendum if needed (owner: legal)
- Support: contact method, SLA summary, escalation path (owner: support)
- Technical artifacts: architecture diagram, network ports list, minimum infra reqs (owner: solutions eng)
- QA: e2e provisioning test, billing test, teardown test (owner: QA)

UX copy snippets (tile -> short -> long) — experiments to pick from (try variant A and variant B in shelf tests):
- Tile title Variant 1: "Redwood Inference — Fast inference API"
- Tile title Variant 2: "Redwood Inference — Production LLM inference"

- Short description Variant 1 (25–60 chars): "Low-latency, cost-aware LLM inference in the cloud"
- Short description Variant 2: "Serve LLMs with predictable latency and spend"

- Long description Variant 1 (1–2 paragraphs):
  "Redwood Inference provides a unified runtime for serving large language models across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Ship features faster with production-grade throughput, transparent performance profiles, and rollout controls (canary, A/B). Start with a free trial and scale to reserved capacity."

- Long description Variant 2:
  "Ship LLM features with confidence. Redwood combines an optimized serving runtime, intelligent batching, and routing policies to balance latency and unit economics. Choose hosted API for speed, Dedicated pools for predictable throughput, or Private deployments for compliance-sensitive workloads."

Copy tone notes: emphasize pragmatic, engineering-first claims; avoid strong comparative language (we're not the review page copy). Use measurable claims where possible (e.g., "predictable latency at scale" vs vague superlatives).

UX constraints and compliance snippets (text we can paste into listing fields):
- Customer-facing privacy blurb: "We process customer prompts and metadata to provide inference services. Customers can opt into or request deletion of stored artifacts. See our DPA for details."
- Billing blurb (short): "Billing is metered via tokens and capacity commitments. See SKU details for trial vs reserved tiers."
- Technical note for detail page: "Supports SAML/OIDC SSO, KMS integrations, and private VPC peering for Private deployments. Contact sales for Dedicated capacity sizing."

Technical packaging and artifact checklist (engineering items):
- Provide a digestible architecture PDF (one page) for the listing assets.
- Endpoint examples: curl and SDK snippet (JS + Python) with sample response and latency expectation.
- Minimum GPU/CPU profile for Dedicated sizing table.
- Installable artifacts for Private: container image tag, helm chart values example, KMS integration snippet.

Security & legal gating details (avoid bureaucratic novel):
- Minimum required certification for enterprise listing: SOC2 Type II or equivalent. If not available, provide a security questionnaire + mitigation plan.
- Data residency claim must be explicit: list the supported cloud regions and whether PII is ever persisted.
- KMS: list supported providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, customer HSM). Provide sample KMS policy.

Preflight test matrix (what QA runs):
- Onboarding flow: sign-up via marketplace -> service provision -> sample request -> success response (monitor for token usage).
- Billing: purchase via marketplace SKU -> invoice generated -> trial expired -> upgrade path.
- SSO: SAML test with Okta test tenant -> login succeeded -> role mapping verified.
- Private deployment smoke: local install -> start services -> healthcheck endpoints respond.

Ownership and runway (who to ping):
- PM (listing content + acceptance): Sana Kapoor
- Design (tile + screenshots): Mateo Rivera
- Solutions/SE (arch + packaging): Elliot Park
- Security: Priya Shah (for gating sign-offs)
- Legal: Jordan Mills

Open questions / TODOs:
- Pricing model for trial vs reserved: need finance sign-off (JIRA-GO-4789)
- Screenshot assets: need 2 hero images (one for hosted API flow, one for Dedicated) — Mateo to iterate
- Table of supported model families and quantization options — product to publish
- Localization: should we publish EN-only for first release? likely yes.

Hand-off checklist for Confluence runbook (what to move when this is stable):
- Copy variants and chosen A/B winners
- Final acceptance matrix mapped to owners + Jira tasks
- Artifact bundle: short architecture pdf, 2 screenshots, curl/SDK snippets, admin guide link
- Post-launch monitoring plan: listing telemetry to capture (clicks -> signup -> conversion)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally compact. If you're reviewing and think a required item is missing, add it as a line above with an owner and Jira ticket.
- For the first marketplace push target AWS and GCP; add Azure once we have ARM packaging for Private.

Quick decision log (live):
- 2024-11-05: created (Ava)
- 2024-11-10: chosen long description Variant 2 for first draft (PM sync)
- 2024-11-22: added KMS policy example link (github PR 62)

Small UX experiment ideas for launch week:
- Variant A tile that mentions "free trial" vs Variant B that mentions "reserved capacity" to see which drives lead quality.
- Short survey in listing to capture intended deployment (hosted/dedicated/private) — low friction button on detail page.

End of lab — please leave inline comments or add to linked Jira for anything that needs formal follow-up.
